newsitem.title: FRANCE: French ex-minister calls on Mandela over Zaire.
newsitem.headline: French ex-minister calls on Mandela over Zaire.

text.p: A former French minister who championed the right to intervention on humanitarian grounds called on South African President Nelson Mandela on Monday to step in to try avert a human disaster in eastern Zaire.
"Mr President, you are the only African leader whose moral weight and military power can force destiny," former Socialist humanitarian affairs minister Benard Kouchner wrote in the daily Le Monde.

In a separate statement, the medical charity Doctors without Borders (MsF) called for an international task force to set up protection zones for more than a millon mostly Hutu refugees caught in fighting between Zairean forces and Tutsi rebels, backed by Rwanda's Tutsi army, and facing starvation after aid agencies pulled out.
"Can we let them die?" Kouchner asked.
He said France, for diplomatic reasons, and the United States, because of its imminent presidential election, would not intervene.
"You are the only one today able to initiate and even start an emergency military intervention to restore peace," he said.

"Only you can convince the (warring) parties to attend the Nairobi conference called for Tuesday. The right to intervention, so criticised by the conservatives, remains the only way of protecting minorities from death," he said.
"The solution is not a humanitarian one. It is a diplomatic and military one. Humanitarian corridors and the refugees must be protected militarily," he said.

South Africa said on Monday it would cancel its 87 million rand ($18.5 million) arms deal with Rwanda if asked to do so by leaders at Tuesday's African summit, where East and Central African leaders are scheduled to discuss the worsening situation in eastern Zaire.
